title: PIMPAL: Accelerating LLM Inference on Edge Devices via In-DRAM Arithmetic Lookup
problem: Accelerating LLM inference on edge devices; General Matrix-Vector Multiplication (GEMV) is memory-intensive and difficult to accelerate with conventional edge computing; existing PIM architectures suffer from high area overhead or restricted computational precision.
motivation: Large Language Models deployed on edge devices (sLLMs) require efficient GEMV acceleration; conventional processing units in PIM architectures incur high area costs; simpler computational primitives (LUTs) can reduce area while maintaining performance.
method: Instead of doing arithmetic in a processor, PIMPAL pre-computes and stores the results of calculations as lookup tables inside DRAM memory, then looks up these values in parallel across multiple sections of DRAM banks. This avoids the energy cost of moving data back and forth between memory and a processor. The system uses smart data placement to minimize DRAM row activations (the expensive operation of reading different parts of memory), and combines results from multiple small lookup tables to support multiple precision levels.
key_novelty: PIMPAL uses lookup tables stored in DRAM memory instead of traditional arithmetic operations to accelerate matrix-vector multiplication with low chip area overhead while supporting multiple precision levels on edge devices.
contributions: PIMPAL PIM architecture leveraging parallel in-DRAM LUT lookups for GEMV
Locality-aware Compute Mapping to minimize row activations
LUT Aggregation mechanism enabling multi-precision computations
17.8x higher performance than prior LUT-based PIM; 40% area reduction vs. processing unit-based PIM
